THE FRONTLINE

This is the most important line in the world.

It’s the line Ukraine is holding between a free Europe and a dictatorship trying to redraw its borders by force. What happens here will shape Ukraine’s future, Europe’s security and the world we live in long after this war is over.

And yet almost nobody has ever seen the full picture.

Every frontline report focuses on one place. One village. One battle. One weapon.

And then the camera leaves.

I want to show you the whole picture.

For the first time, I’ll be driving across the entire region to create a comprehensive documentary series about this war as one connected journey.

Thousands of kilometres along the road through a country fighting the biggest invasion Europe has faced since the Second World War.

I want to connect all of it.

Because these aren’t separate battles in separate towns.

They’re chapters of one enormous story.

A war stretching across hundreds of kilometres. Millions of lives caught inside it. And a frontline that has become one of the great fault lines of our time.

And I won’t be doing it alone.

I’m teaming up with Zarina Zabrisky, an incredible American journalist and writer who has spent years reporting from Kherson and southern Ukraine. I’ve known Zarina since 2019, when we made our first reports together. Now, we’re getting back on the road for the biggest project we’ve ever attempted.

We’ll be reporting as we go and bringing you new stories throughout the journey.

This is the most ambitious independent reporting project I’ve ever attempted.

And I need your help to get it on the road.

It’s being commissioned by you.

I don’t take government money. I don’t take sponsorships. And there isn’t a shady billionaire somewhere quietly paying for all of this. It’s you.

Every film I make is possible because people watching my films choose to support them, particularly the incredible community that has grown around my Patreon.

This journey is different because of its scale.

A car capable of making the journey. Thousands of kilometres of petrol. Accommodation. Protective equipment. Fixers and translators. Communications. Camera equipment. Insurance. Storage. Repairs. And all the things you can’t predict until you’re thousands of kilometres from home and something inevitably breaks.

We need to raise around $10,000 to make it happen.

If you’ve ever watched one of my reports and thought, more people need to see this, you can help me make the biggest one yet.

And if you help fund the project, your name can appear in the credits of the final film as one of the people who made it possible.

This isn’t being commissioned by a television network.
